newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-INDIANS CLINCH TITLE, YANKEES AND ORIOLES RAINED OUT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-INDIANS CLINCH TITLE, YANKEES AND ORIOLES RAINED OUT.

text.p: The Cleveland Indians clinched their second straight American League Central Division title Tuesday as Kevin Seitzer blasted a grand slam and Manny Ramirez had four hits and three RBI in a 9-4 victory over the Chicago White Sox.

Cleveland (91-59), which has won eight of its last nine games, became the first major-league team to qualify for the post-season. It is the first time in the 96-year history of the club it has reached the playoffs in consecutive seasons.

"In some ways it has been a very difficult year, but in some ways it has also been one of the most satisfying years I've been inlvolved with," Indians manager Mike Hargrove said. "Things really came together for us after the All-Star break and these guys are all winners."

The Indians jumped on Alex Fernandez (14-10) in the first inning as Jim Thome, Albert Belle, Julio Franco and Ramirez singled with two out to plate two runs. Franco stole home on the front end of a double steal to make it 3-0.

After Frank Thomas's 37th homer -- his fifth in three games -- cut it to 3-1, Cleveland added five more runs in the second, capped by Seitzer's 13th homer and fourth career grand slam to make it 7-1. Ramirez got an RBI single one out later.

"It was a pretty good pitch, it was a changeup, the same pitch he made me look stupid on before," Seitzer said. "But this one he got up, and I got a hold of it. Right now I just want to enjoy the moment and tomorrow I'll put it behind me and begin to think about the post-season."
Brian Anderson (3-1) won his third straight decision, allowing three runs, seven hits and one walk with two strikeouts over six innings.

Cleveland's Albert Belle, who was 3-for-5, recorded the 1,000th hit of his career. Kenny Lofton's single in the second was his 200th hit of the season, making him the first Indians left-handed hitter to get 200 since Dale Mitchell in 1949.
The White Sox have dropped six of their last eight games and fell 3 1/2 games behind Baltimore for the wild-card berth.
In New York, the scheduled challenge by the second-place Baltimore Orioles of the A.L. East-leading Yankees was postponed due to rain. The game was rescheduled as part of a doubleheader Thursday.

In Detroit, Jose Canseco, just activated off the disabled list, drew a bases-loaded walk in the seventh to lift the Boston Red Sox to a 4-2 victory over the Tigers, who absorbed their 100th loss of the season.
Boston is 5 1/2 games behind Baltimore in the wild-car race.
Detroit second baseman Mark Lewis left the game in the third inning after being hit in the head with a pitch.
In Seattle, Terry Mulholland allowed two runs over 6 1/3 innings and Dave Hollins had a two-run single in a four-run sixth inning as the Mariners won their sixth straight, 5-2 over the Texas Rangers.
Mulholland (5-2) won for the fourth time in his last five starts, allowing four hits and no walks with three strikeouts.
The Mariners, who have won eight of 11 meetings with Texas this season, pulled within four games of the A.L. West-leading Rangers and three games of Baltimore for the wild card spot.

In Kansas City, Chris Haney allowed two runs over seven innings and Chris Stynes's RBI groundout in the fifth inning snapped a tie as the Royals defeated the Minnesota Twins 4-2 for their fourth straight victory.
Haney (10-14) stopped a personal four-game losing skid and a six-start winless streak. He allowed eight hits, did not walk a batter and struck out five.
Mike Macfarlane homered for Kansas City.
The Twins' Paul Molitor, who reached the 3,000-hit milestone in Monday's loss, had a pinch-hit single in the ninth.
In Milwaukee, Ben McDonald scattered three hits over eight innings and Fernando Vina had a two-run triple as the Brewers blanked the Toronto Blue Jays 4-0, snapping a four-game home losing streak.
McDonald (12-10) walked one and fanned a season-high 10 as he won his second straight start.
At California, emergency starter Ariel Prieto scattered seven hits over 6 2/3 innings and Terry Steinbach and Brian Lesher hit back-to-back homers as the Oakland Athletics defeated the Angels 5-1.
Prieto started in place of Willie Adams, who had a sore right shoulder, and walked three and fanned eight.
Oakland won its second straight game despite being held to just five hits. California has lost seven straight and 10 of 11. The Angels have allowed 32 runs in their last four games.
